paper.title: CLOT: Closed-Loop Global Motion Tracking for Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, 2026-02-20; latest public arXiv version verified 2026-08-30. Official code evidence pinned to efcea1cf252d4164ece4d90b6d0e3211b5f1814f.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: CLOT explicitly decouples the future reference presented to the actor from the current reference used by the tracking reward, reports task-reward components and independent motion/torque metrics, and exposes a useful boundary between an oracle edit and a trainer-observation edit.
not_evidence_for: automatic motion-clip selection or reference-graph composition
an OGMP-style state machine or receding-horizon oracle
a reference-only intervention under a frozen observation contract
a stateless executable AMP task-reward function
VIBE integration or a frozen foundation controller

mechanisms.name: Global closed-loop whole-body tracking
mechanisms.description: Online IK-retargeted human motion supplies robot reference commands while high-rate external localization supplies measured robot global pose; the policy produces joint-position targets that a low-level PD controller executes.

mechanisms.name: Randomized observation pre-shift
mechanisms.description: During training, the reference window in the actor observation is randomly shifted to a future temporal offset while the physical state and history remain at the current time. The mechanism is disabled at inference.

mechanisms.name: Current-time reward alignment
mechanisms.description: Even when the actor sees a future-shifted goal window, tracking reward is evaluated against the original target at the current timestep. Observation and reward therefore have distinct reference clocks.

mechanisms.name: Weighted tracking and safety task reward
mechanisms.description: The task reward combines exponentially decaying tracking kernels for body, keypoint, foot, joint, and contact objectives with control, contact, limit, collision, and early-termination penalties.

mechanisms.name: Adversarial motion-prior reward
mechanisms.description: A learned discriminator supplies log D_phi(s_t) as a style reward, combined with task reward through lambda_style and lambda_task. It requires style data and a discriminator optimization loop.

mechanisms.name: Transformer actor-critic
mechanisms.description: Actor and critic tokenize historical states, current proprioception, and tracking goals and process them with three Transformer blocks to model the temporal mismatch induced by pre-shift.

mechanisms.name: Tracking, control, and task evaluation suite
mechanisms.description: Evaluation separates global/local body tracking, root and joint error, mean and temporal variability of torque, task success rate, and completion time from the training reward.

mechanisms.name: Contact- and kinematics-curated human motion corpus
mechanisms.description: The training references come from about twenty hours of motion captured under a protocol intended to preserve contact consistency and compatibility with humanoid kinematics.

failure_modes.name: Aggressive global-error correction
failure_modes.description: The authors report that strong global tracking objectives can conflict with local joint objectives, drive rapid error minimization, produce excessive torque, and converge to unsafe or suboptimal behavior.

failure_modes.name: Accumulated global pose drift
failure_modes.description: Local-frame trackers lack global pose closure, so global trajectory errors accumulate during long-horizon operation according to the paper's motivating analysis.

failure_modes.name: Under-specified pre-shift distribution
failure_modes.description: The paper leaves T_max_pre and the sampling probability numerical values unstated. Its appendix range [1,2] is not unambiguously mapped to delta, and pinned release defaults differ by robot.

failure_modes.name: Full-system ablation conflates components
failure_modes.description: Table II compares Transformer-only with the full system, jointly changing observation pre-shift and motion-prior machinery. Table III isolates pre-shift only for abrupt-error recovery statistics.

failure_modes.name: External global-localization dependency
failure_modes.description: The real feedback loop depends on OptiTrack. The conclusion identifies lightweight global localization and VR motion tracking as future work.

failure_modes.name: Only part of the training corpus is public
failure_modes.description: The paper reports about twenty hours of captured motion; the pinned official README says about ten hours have been uploaded.

failure_modes.name: Narrow baseline coverage
failure_modes.description: TWIST2 is compared on G1 simulation only; MPC is compared on real T1 only; T2 and T3 have no baseline; the external-kick evaluation is qualitative.

failure_modes.name: Pre-shift violates a frozen-observation comparison
failure_modes.description: For Sam's harness, pre-shift is not a pure reference-composition change if the oracle interface does not already authorize changing the actor's observation target and training distribution.

evaluation.name: G1 held-out motion comparison
evaluation.description: On the held-out simulation corpus, CLOT reports lower four tracking errors and torque variability than TWIST2, while mean torque is slightly higher.

evaluation.name: Adam Pro full versus Transformer-only comparison
evaluation.description: The full system reports lower tracking errors, mean torque, and torque variability than the Transformer-only variant, but the contrast changes more than one component.

evaluation.name: Abrupt-reference pre-shift recovery ablation
evaluation.description: With pre-shift, absolute mean joint torque and DOF velocity have lower reported standard deviation and smoothness statistics during abrupt reference-error recovery.

evaluation.name: Transformer versus MLP at 2.0-second pre-shift
evaluation.description: The paper's qualitative trajectory comparison reports stable Transformer tracking and an MLP fall at a 2.0-second shift.

evaluation.name: Three real loco-manipulation tasks
evaluation.description: Thirty trials per task report 27, 24, and 26 CLOT successes for T1, T2, and T3; only T1 includes an MPC baseline with 20 successes.

evaluation.name: Thirty-minute uninterrupted teleoperation
evaluation.description: The paper samples tracking errors at one hertz during a thirty-minute real run and reports stable bounded distributions, without numerical means in rendered text.

evaluation.name: Independent kinematic and torque metrics
evaluation.description: The appendix defines global/local body error, root error, joint error, mean absolute joint torque, and temporal torque variability as evaluation metrics.

relations.target: Unitree G1 and PNDbotics Adam Pro

evidence.locator: Abstract and submission history
evidence.claim: The record identifies the paper, reports over 1300 GPU hours and a 31-DoF full-sized humanoid, and lists v2 on 20 February 2026 as the latest public version.

evidence.locator: Section III-A, Problem Formulation
evidence.claim: The controller is a goal-conditioned PPO policy with a 23-dimensional joint-target action.

evidence.locator: Sections III-B and III-C; Table I
evidence.claim: The authors captured about twenty hours of motion under contact and kinematic constraints and retarget it with whole-body IK.

evidence.locator: Section III-D, Basic Components for RL Training; Equation 2
evidence.claim: The actor uses a ten-step future goal window and ten-step history; tracking rewards use exp(-err/sigma).

evidence.locator: Section III-E.1, Observation Pre-shift; Equation 3
evidence.claim: Training randomly future-shifts the actor reference window while reward stays aligned with the current target; pre-shift is disabled at inference.

evidence.locator: Sections III-E.2 and III-E.3; Equations 4-6
evidence.claim: CLOT uses Transformer actor and critic networks and combines learned AMP style reward with task reward through a discriminator objective.

evidence.locator: Section III-F, Closed-Loop Real-World Teleoperation System
evidence.claim: OptiTrack runs at 120 Hz, Hi5 finger capture at 60 Hz, policy at 50 Hz, and the PD controller at 400 Hz.

evidence.locator: Appendix Table V, Reward Terms and Their Weights
evidence.claim: The table enumerates twelve positive coefficients and twelve penalty coefficients used in RL training.

evidence.locator: Appendix Table VI, Observation Details
evidence.claim: The table gives complete observation tensor dimensions, including ten future references and ten history steps over 29 body points.

evidence.locator: Appendix Table VIII, Curriculum Learning Parameters
evidence.claim: The Observation Pre-shift row reports sigma 5e-6 and range [1,2] without units.

evidence.locator: Appendix Table IX, Neural Network Architecture Parameters
evidence.claim: Actor and critic use a 192-dimensional, four-head, three-block Transformer with 768-dimensional feedforward layers; the discriminator is a four-layer 1024-unit MLP.

evidence.locator: Appendix Table X, PD Controller Parameters
evidence.claim: The table lists fixed Adam Pro proportional and derivative gains by joint class.

evidence.locator: Appendix B-A, Experiment Setup
evidence.claim: Final policy training used eight RTX 4090 GPUs for approximately one week in MJLab.

evidence.locator: Section IV-A and Table II, Simulation Performance Comparison
evidence.claim: The paper reports held-out G1 CLOT/TWIST2 results and Adam full/Transformer-only results over four tracking and two torque metrics.

evidence.locator: Table III and Figure 6, Observation Pre-shift Ablation
evidence.claim: With pre-shift, abrupt-error recovery has lower reported joint-torque and DOF-velocity fluctuation and smoothness statistics.

evidence.locator: Section IV-A.2 and Figure 7, Network Architecture Ablation
evidence.claim: At a 2.0-second pre-shift, the paper reports stable Transformer tracking while the MLP fails and falls.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B.1 and Table IV, Real Task Performance
evidence.claim: The table reports thirty-trial success and average success time for three real tasks, with an MPC comparison only on T1.

evidence.locator: Section IV-B.2 and Figure 8, Long-horizon Teleoperation Stability
evidence.claim: The authors ran thirty minutes uninterrupted, sampled tracking errors at one hertz, and report bounded distributions without numerical text summaries.

evidence.locator: Appendix B-B, Evaluation Metrics
evidence.claim: The appendix defines global/local body, root, joint, mean-torque, and torque-variability metrics.

evidence.locator: Section V, Conclusion
evidence.claim: Future work targets lightweight global localization and VR-based human motion tracking.

evidence.locator: Official README at efcea1c, lines 74-125
evidence.claim: The release states that about ten hours are uploaded, defaults to eight RTX 4090 GPUs, and exposes MLP, Transformer, and AMP experiment variants.

evidence.locator: Official Adam domain-randomization YAML at efcea1c, lines 112-120
evidence.claim: The pinned Adam default enables motion-time advance and declares a [0.5,1.5] second offset range.

evidence.locator: Official G1 domain-randomization YAML at efcea1c, lines 115-123
evidence.claim: The pinned G1 default disables motion-time advance while declaring the same [0.5,1.5] second offset range.
